about: New Zealand-based commercial airlines and the aircraft types they fly, for painting each airline's real livery on each type. Edit freely: add an airline or type and re-run tools/build_livery_prompts.py. 'key' becomes the file suffix (a320-anz.webp). Counts are approximate; sources are listed per airline.
style_ref_line: Image 1 is the STYLE reference: match its style, line weight, palette, level of detail and cream ground exactly, but do NOT copy its aircraft type or livery.
repaint_line: Image 1 is the APPROVED AIRFRAME for this aircraft type. Keep its shape, proportions, number of wings, engines and tail surfaces, pose and woodblock line style EXACTLY as drawn. Change ONLY the paint scheme.
not_included: Fleets not verified, so left out: Parcelair (Freightways, 2 Boeing 737 freighters per Wikipedia, undated), Texel Air, Sunair, Golden Bay Air, Air Safaris, Glenorchy Air, Air Kaikoura, Air Napier, Salt Air and other small Cessna / GippsAero GA8 operators. International airlines flying into New Zealand are covered by 'plane_illustrations.py --sightings', which finds the airline and type of everything actually seen overhead.

prompts.side:
Generate a side-profile view of an Airbus A320-200 (ICAO type A320) in the style of an Edo-period Japanese woodblock print, painted as carefully as a kacho-e bird. Render with VERY FEW MARKS: the aircraft is 2-4 flat colour zones with sharp boundaries, no rivets, no panel lines, no windows drawn one by one. Confident sumi-e ink linework, soft watercolour washes. Earthy palette: burnt umber, ochre, indigo, vermillion, muted greens. Painted in the real, current livery of Air New Zealand: its actual colour scheme, tail design and fuselage markings, simplified into flat woodblock colour zones so the airline is instantly recognisable. Include the airline's name and logo where the real aircraft carries them, drawn in the same woodblock style. NO registration marks and no other lettering.

The aircraft sits on a CONSISTENT WARM CREAM ground (aged mulberry paper), filling the frame, identical across every print. This is the only background: NO sky, NO clouds, NO runway, NO ground, NO scenery. NO text or lettering anywhere in the image except the airline's own name and logo on the aircraft itself; NO registration marks.

- Correct anatomy for an Airbus A320-200: the right number and position of engines, wings, tail surfaces and landing gear (or rotors and skids) as the real type has them.
- Side profile, level flight, undercarriage retracted (skids or wheels tucked for a helicopter: show it in a steady hover). Nose to the right.
